problem: Existing VLN benchmarks focus on route-following to a fixed goal and give little controlled evaluation of conditional (if-then-else) instructions whose branch depends on observed scene state, so failures cannot be attributed to perception, grounding, navigation or logic.
motivation: Real navigation instructions often depend on environment state (e.g., 'if there is a coffee table in the kitchen, go to X, otherwise Y'). Deciding this requires evaluating scene evidence, picking the right branch and executing it. Scene graphs make condition truth values verifiable, enabling controlled diagnosis.
key_idea: Programmatically generate conditional VLN instructions from 3D scene-graph predicates with controllable branch depth and chain length, and evaluate with branch-specific metrics (BSA, CSR) alongside SR/SPL.
insight: Agents can reach plausible goals (nontrivial SR) while committing to the wrong branch, so BSA/CSR are much lower than SR and standard metrics hide this. The depth/chain scaling table shows BSA and especially CSR degrade as depth or chain length increases. The symbolic oracle branch resolution helps most at higher complexity (e.g., d=3,l=1 CSR 17.63 vs Open-Nav 12.27), but not consistently in the aggregate, since it is an oracle probe rather than a real reasoner.
method: Scene hierarchy input: unify AI2-THOR, ReplicaCAD, MP3D and Gibson annotations into rooms containing objects with labels, 3D centers and optional AABB/radius.

Spatial/semantic relation generation: per-room directed graphs with 8-sector azimuth x up/level/down canonical predicates, plus thresholded near/far, higher/lower, above/below; distance uses AABB -> sphere -> center fallback.

Conditional instruction synthesis: IF-condition-THEN-ELSE templates over object presence, with valid and invalid (absent-from-room) objects for true/false branches. Objects are disambiguated with spatial qualifiers. Complexity varies over nesting depth (1-3) and chain length (1-3), giving six categories.
VLN-CE realization: convert to R2R/VLN-CE JSON episodes in Habitat, with geodesic reference paths via the pathfinder and filtering of failed paths.
Metrics: BSA = fraction of ordered branch subgoals reached in order; CSR = 1 only if BSA=1 and standard success.
Oracle neurosymbolic baseline: use recorded symbolic metadata to rewrite the conditional instruction into a linear 'go to g_b' (or ordered subgoal chain) and pass it to an unchanged VLN-Zero.

setting.backbone: Evaluated agents: VLN-Zero, NaVid, NaVILA, Open-Nav (existing models, no retraining); Oracle = VLN-Zero with oracle-linearized instructions
setting.training_data: none (benchmark; agents evaluated without retraining; oracle is a deterministic instruction rewrite)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB(-D) in Habitat VLN-CE-compatible setting
setting.action_space: low-level VLN-CE continuous-environment actions (agent-dependent), fixed action budget proportional to instruction length
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE-compatible) on AI2-THOR, ReplicaCAD, Gibson, MP3D scenes
setting.privileged: Oracle baseline uses ground-truth branch and subgoal annotations from scene graph; other agents none

numbers.extra: uses GT branch selection; averaged over all instruction categories

numbers_note: The benchmark is new (no canonical name), so entries use other:CondNav-style labels; split named 'test' is an assumption since the paper does not name splits. Baseline rows (NaVid, NaVILA, Open-Nav) are omitted per the rules. Depth/chain scaling numbers (Table 3) are aggregated over datasets and not included.
results: NaVid and NaVILA nearly fail (CSR 0-11), whereas Open-Nav and VLN-Zero are stronger (e.g., AI2-THOR CSR 29.9 and 21.0). SR is markedly higher than BSA/CSR in general. The oracle branch resolver does not dominate in aggregate but does in harder regimes (d=3: CSR 17.63 vs Open-Nav 12.27 and VLN-Zero 10.08), which the abstract summarizes as a 2x improvement.
limitations: The neurosymbolic baseline is an oracle using ground-truth scene-graph branch info, so it is not a real perception-driven agent and gains are an upper-bound probe.
Restricted to VLN-CE-compatible indoor simulators; inherits scan/annotation noise and fixed geometric heuristics for relations.
Absolute numbers are small and unstable (e.g., Gibson), with no stated episode counts or variance in the text.
